info.title: CarsMultiverse - the recall record
info.summary: Vehicle safety recalls across five national registers, and whether a notice was reworded after it was published.
info.description:
Two things here are not published anywhere else.

1. THE CROSSWALK. Recalls proven to appear in more than one country's register, matched on the manufacturer's own campaign code after identical normalisation. No regulator holds more than its own register. Nothing is paired on brand and date.

2. THE REWRITE RECORD. Recall notices are edited after publication and the registers keep no public history. This site re-reads the wording and keeps every version, so it can say what a notice said before, what it says now, and when each reading was taken.

Everything is CC BY 4.0. Credit carsmultiverse.com. The crosswalk has a DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22087135.

get.summary: What we hold for one campaign, including whether it was reworded
get.description:
Note the three-valued answer. `rewritten` is true, false, or null - and null is NOT a no. Null means the campaign sits outside the watched set, so no comparison has been made. Not knowing and knowing it did not happen are different facts, and an agent that collapses them will state something false.

Where a rewrite is held, `rewrites[].first_read` is when we read the earlier wording and `rewrites[].read` is when we read the changed wording. The change happened between those two times.

200.description: Revisions, each with before, after, before_read and after_read. The field named 'summary' here is the defect description - the same text the /wp-json/cmvreg/v1/changes endpoint calls 'defect'. One field, two names, verified identical; do not treat a change reported by both as two changes.
